claims.text: A film of 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2-like high-entropy-alloy nanoflakes can be applied by spray coating.
Spray-coated 2D HEA nanoflakes on CoCrFeNi will reduce friction consistently from room temperature to 800 °C.
Spray-coated 2D HEA nanoflakes on CoCrFeNi will reduce wear consistently from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed coating will remain effective under variable loads.
The proposed coating will remain effective under variable environments.
Unmodified coarse-grained CoCrFeNi exhibits moderate-to-high friction and wear during dry sliding over variable temperatures.
Frictional stress or energy can activate tribocatalytic behavior in the (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes.
Elevated temperature activates tribocatalytic reactions in the nanoflake coating.
The nanoflakes catalyze formation of a dense, nanocrystalline tribolayer on CoCrFeNi.
The resulting tribolayer may incorporate lubricious oxides.
The resulting tribolayer may incorporate amorphous carbon.
A self-organized tribolayer lowers the effective shear strength of the sliding interface.
The tribolayer protects the substrate from adhesive, oxidative, and plastic wear.
Compared with uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated samples will have lower and more stable coefficients of friction at both low and high temperatures.
Compared with uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated samples will have lower specific wear rates at both low and high temperatures.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has variable friction and increased wear at high temperatures and varying loads because its oxide films are unstable and lubrication is insufficient.
The intervention is expected to be effective specifically under dry sliding in ambient air.
Nanoflake tribological performance depends on the coating formulation or surrounding chemical environment.
Long-term tribolayer durability over repeated cycles and extreme thermal gradients is uncertain.
A controlled ball-on-disk comparison at 5 N and 30 N from room temperature to 800 °C can test the coating by measuring friction, wear, and tribolayer formation.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims effectiveness under variable environments, whereas the specified tests and asserted effectiveness are limited to ambient air, and performance in vacuum or corrosive atmospheres is expressly left unverified.
